summary: This paper presents an interesting framework for combining proactive behavior, approval workflows, and external reasoning in Discord-based AI agents. The empirical evaluation is thorough and shows significant improvements across multiple dimensions.
strengths: Clear motivation and well-defined problem statement
Comprehensive experimental design with multiple user studies
Strong statistical significance in reported results
Good balance between system description and empirical evaluation
Clear ablation study showing contribution of each component
weaknesses: Related work section could be more comprehensive, particularly regarding prior work on proactive AI assistants
Limited discussion of ethical considerations beyond basic safety
No exploration of failure cases or limitations of the approval workflow in practice
The paper would benefit from a more detailed discussion of scalability to large servers
Some claims about novelty could be better substantiated with more precise comparisons to existing work
questions: How does the system handle concurrent users requesting different actions?
What happens if a user never responds to an approval request?
Have you considered alternative approval mechanisms beyond simple yes/no?
How does the proactive behavior scale with server size and message volume?
What are the computational costs of integrating with NotebookLM?
missing_references: Work on proactive assistants in mobile contexts (e.g., Google Now, Siri suggestions)
Research on human-AI collaboration and shared control
Studies on notification fatigue and optimal timing for proactive interventions
